previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with left-sided chest pain radiating to the abdomen and back, associated with shortness of breath, nausea, and dizziness. Initial evaluation revealed a supratherapeutic INR of 4.3 and severe iron deficiency anemia with a hemoglobin of 7.8 g/dL. A CTA showed an infrarenal aortic ulceration, managed conservatively with INR correction and blood pressure control. She underwent upper endoscopy and colonoscopy, which identified gastritis and diverticulosis as likely sources of occult gastrointestinal bleeding, though no active bleeding was seen. She received two units of packed red blood cells and was started on iron supplementation. Her chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, and her hypoxia, likely due to atelectasis and heart strain, improved with diuresis; however, she was discharged on 2 liters of oxygen with exertion. She was stabilized on adjusted warfarin, continued heart failure and GERD medications, and provided with discharge instructions including follow-up for INR monitoring and iron repletion.

Primary: Gastrointestinal bleed, secondary to NSAID use and 
supratherapeutic INR
Secondary: chronic systolic congestive heart failure
Myofascial pain syndrome

 
Discharge Condition:
Good, hemodynamically stable.  Respiratory status at baseline.

 
Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital because you were bleeding from 
your bowels.  Because of this, you were given blood and you had 
two procedures, an endoscopy and colonoscopy.  You were found to 
have inflammation of your esophagus and stomach (esophagitis and 
gastritis).  Your increased INR (anticoagulation from the 
coumadin) and taking Advil played a role in the bleed.  It is 
important for you to have your anticoagulation levels checked 
regularly to make sure that this does not happen in the future.

Also, while you were here in the hospital, you had some 
difficulty breathing.  This was due to fluid building up in your 
lungs.  We gave you a medication called furosemide (lasix) to 
remove the fluid from your lungs.   You have been prescribed 
this medication to take once you leave the hospital.  It will be 
important for you to continue taking this medication, and to 
weigh yourself every morning to see if you have fluid building 
up. Call your doctor if your weight gain more than 3 lbs.  
Adhere to 2 gm sodium diet.
.
Also, while you were in the hospital, you fell and hit your hand 
and your knee.  Xrays did not show any acute fractures.  You 
were given a splint for your hand, keep it on until you are seen 
by orthopedics.  You will need repeat Xray on ___. 
Physical therapy evaluated you for this, and gave you a walker.  
It is very important that you use your walker at all times while 
walking, as it is unsafe for you to walk without it.
.
Finally, you continued to have chest pain.  Your pain is 
musculoskeletal in nature and is not because of your heart.  
However, if your chest pain changes or becomes much more severe, 
be sure to contact your primary care provider or go to the 
emergency room.  For the chest pain you currently have, we have 
given you percocet and lidocaine patches.
.
Please take all medications as prescribed.  You have been 
discharged with the following changes in your medication:  Your 
Metoprolol 50mg has been changed to Metoprolol XL 25mg daily.
.
Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight > 3 lbs.
Adhere to 2 gm sodium diet
.
Please keep all of your follow up appointments and continue to 
follow up in ___ clinic.
.
If you begin vomiting blood, have large bloody bowel movements 
or have stool that looks entirely black, or have fevers, chest 
pain or trouble breathing, call your primary care provider or go 
to the emergency room.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with GI bleed.

Portable upright AP chest is compared to ___.  The cardiac silhouette is
enlarged.  Widening of the vascular pedicle and perihilar haziness in
combination with increasing small pleural effusions are all consistent with
moderate congestive heart failure.  No definite consolidation is evident.  No
pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  Moderate congestive heart failure, worse when compared to ___ examination.

INDICATION:  Patient is an ___ female with history of elevated INR.
Evaluate for hemorrhage.

EXAMINATION:  Non-contrast head CT.

COMPARISONS:  Comparison to the head CT from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain.  No
intravenous contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, masses, mass effect, or
acute infarction.  The gray-white matter differentiation is preserved.  There
is extensive periventricular hypodensity, compatible with chronic small vessel
ischemic changes.  The ventricles and sulci demonstrate stable prominence,
compatible with age-related involutional changes, with a slight predominance
of atrophic changes within the bilateral frontal lobes.  No acute fracture is
identified.  The visualized portions of the paranasal sinuses and mastoid air
cells are well aerated.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of hemorrhage.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with GI bleed.  Very tender abdomen. Evaluate
for free air or evidence of perforation.

COMPARISON:  None.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable supine and left lateral decubitus abdominal radiographs.

FINDINGS:  No free air is noted on left lateral decubitus views.  Nonspecific
bowel gas pattern is noted on supine views.  Dextroconcave curvature of the
thoracolumbar spine is once again noted.  Indwelling left hip arthroplasty is
once again noted as reported on supine and erect abdominal radiographs dated
___.  Single phlebolith is noted in the pelvis.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of free air noted on left lateral decubitus view.

INDICATION:  History of DVT, please evaluate for DVT since anticoagulation on
hold.

COMPARISON:  ___.

BILATERAL LOWER EXTREMITY VENOUS ULTRASOUND:  Gray-scale and color sonographic
images were obtained that demonstrate wall-to-wall flow with normal response
to respiration and Valsalva in bilateral common femoral veins.  Bilateral
common femoral, superficial, and popliteal veins demonstrate wall-to-wall flow
with normal responses to augmentation and compression.  Right calf veins were
visualized.  Left calf veins were unable to be visualized.

IMPRESSION:  No DVT of the lower extremities with the mild limitation that
left calf veins were not able to be visualized.

EXAM:  Abdomen obtained ___.

___.

HISTORY:  ___ female with abdominal pain, evaluate for free
intraperitoneal air.

FINDINGS:

Supine frontal and left lateral decubitus views of the abdomen were obtained.

There is no evidence of free intraperitoneal air.  Non-dilated loops of
air-filled large bowel are noted throughout the abdomen.  No suspicious
air-fluid levels or calcifications are identified within the abdomen.

Left total hip replacement is partially visualized.  Degenerative changes are
noted within the lower lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of free intraperitoneal air.

2.  Non-obstructive bowel gas pattern.

CHEST TWO VIEWS ON ___

HISTORY:  Left-sided chest pain.

REFERENCE EXAM:  ___.

FINDINGS:  The heart continues to be mildly enlarged with pulmonary vascular
re-distribution and bilateral pleural effusions consistent with fluid
overload.  Compared to the recent study, the fluid overload appears slightly
worse.

NECK FILMS ON ___

HISTORY:  Left chest pain that radiates to the neck.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the neck demonstrate mild degenerative
changes of the spine with some disc space narrowing and vacuum phenomenon,
most marked at C4-5.  The alignment is normal.  No masses are seen.  If
concern for soft tissue mass persists, this would be better assessed with a
different imaging modality such as MRI.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Shortness of breath, questionable pulmonary edema.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, there are unchanged signs
of moderate to severe pulmonary edema.  There is marked cardiomegaly with
retrocardiac atelectasis, small bilateral pleural effusions and generalized
increase of interstitial markings.  Basoapical blood flow re-distribution.  No
focal parenchymal opacities have newly occurred in the interval.

LEFT WRIST, ___

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  History of GI bleed, fall on outstretched hand.

FINDINGS:

Three views of the left wrist are submitted.  There is osteopenia.  An
intravenous line partially obscures the radial styloid.  There is mild osseous
irregularity of the ulnar styloid with possibly erosive change.  This does not
appear to represent an acute fracture.  There is calcification of the
triangular fibrocartilage.  There are mild degenerative changes of the first
CMC and triscaphe joint as well as the first MCP joint.  There is subchondral
cystic change in the lunate.  There are mild degenerative changes at the
radiocarpal joint.  No discrete fractures identified.

RIGHT KNEE, ___

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Mechanical fall, question fracture.

FINDINGS:

Two views of the right knee are submitted.  There is moderate osteoarthritis
of all three compartments of the knee with large osteophytes, joint space
narrowing and subchondral cystic change.  There is probable old fracture
deformity of the tibial eminence with deformity of the tibial spines.  There
is deformity of the lateral femoral condyle with old osteochondral defect.  No
discrete fracture is identified.  There is no joint effusion.  If there is
continuing suspicion for fracture, then MRI or CT may be helpful for further
assessment.
